newsitem.title: INDIA: "Peace in the air" for holidaying Sri Lanka head.
newsitem.headline: "Peace in the air" for holidaying Sri Lanka head.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Bandarnaike Kumaratunga began a holiday in India on Wednesday after Tamil rebels began an undeclared Christmas truce in their 13-year old war, sources on both sides said.
"There is peace in the air. We are confident 1997 will bring good news," one source close to her told Reuters. "Right now she is thinking more about peace than about war."
Indian and Sri Lankan officials played down reports of a link between Kumaratunga's visit and rumoured peace initiatives with the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).

"The president is at present on a private visit to India with her two children," a Sri Lankan Embassy statement said. She will meet Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda at the end of her visit, it added.

The Press Trust of India said Kumaratunga arrived on Wednesday in the western city of Jodhpur where she will spend two days among its historic Rajput palaces. She plans to visit neighbouring Jaisalmer city later for a walk on the sand dunes.
Her visit will be accompanied by tight security and the media are being kept well away.
Kumaratunga arrived in Delhi on Tuesday, two days after the LTTE released 16 captured Sinhalese fishermen as part of a Christmas truce, an LTTE source said.
"This is a normal gesture during Christmas. If you want to read a deeper meaning into it, it's your business," he said.
LTTE sources said Kumaratunga's government had encouraged a peace initiative recently by an international humanitarian group but they gave no details.
They said any progress towards peace with the LTTE would hinge on the government's attitude to rebel leader Velupillai Prabhakaran's latest peace offer in November.
Prabhakaran had demanded the withdrawal of Sri Lankan troops from Tamil areas as one of the conditions for resuming talks with Colombo, they said.
The Indian Express newspaper said on Tuesday there were "reports of impending negotiations with the LTTE through mediators".
But a former Indian diplomat said on Tuesday the reports appeared to have no links with the visit.
"My information is that she had planned to take a holiday from the pressures of the civil war in her country," he said.

India has been closely involved in Sri Lanka's turbulent ethnic crises, providing armed assistance to Colombo in fending off a hardline Sinhalese-led rebellion and later by sending in troops there in a failed attempt in 1987 to disarm the LTTE.
Kumaratunga last visited India for a South Asian summit in May last year.
But she had to cut short her stay at that time after the LTTE shot down an air force plane, signalling a resumption of its 13-year old war against Colombo following a brief truce.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
The Sri Lanka government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the ethnic conflict. The LTTE claims the number is much higher.
